question.problem:
A distance function $s(t)$ has values according to the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $1.0$ | $1.5$ | $2.0$ | $2.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $s(t)$ | $0$ | $3.2$ | $7.5$ | $12.4$ | $17.5$ | $24.3$ |

Approximate the velocity ${s}^{′}(t)$ at the point $t=2.5$ using a backward difference approximation.
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{s}^{′}(t)≈\frac{s(t)-s(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $t=2.5.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=0.5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{′}(2.5) & ≈\frac{s(2.5)-s(2.5-0.5)}{0.5} \\  & =\frac{s(2.5)-s(2.0)}{0.5} \\  & =\frac{24.3-17.5}{0.5} \\  & =\frac{6.8}{0.5} \\  & =13.6.\end{aligned}
$$
